# M3.2 independent quest observer review

Reviewer: research/verification agent, independent of the production implementation and test authors. Scope: the M3.2 changes to `integration/quest`, `PlanningService.planForNext`/`overviewContext`, quest command routing, the unavailable quest-detail graph edge, and the added pure and real-FTB tests. The reviewer did not edit production code or tests, run builds, or interact with the player's game.

## Source review result

**No blocking correctness issue found in the reviewed patch, completed automated/isolated-runtime gates, or focused real-world command retest.** Both the isolated official ATM10 quest book and the user's actual integrated world succeeded through the ordinary-command overview route. The real-world result is supported separately below and is not inferred from the isolated probe.

- **Truth and freshness:** every snapshot resolves the current player's FTB team and existing nullable team data again. There is no cross-request cache of quest definitions, flags, task progress or availability. The original public FTB methods still determine visibility, started/completed flags, dependency satisfaction and task eligibility. The optimization does not infer an AND dependency rule or reinterpret a configured item reference as a complete matching requirement.
- **Explicit overview projection:** normal `/companion quests` and `/companion next` requests use the distinct `QuestOverview` DTO. It collects current counts and at most five available option titles; it explicitly says task progress, dependency edges and full details were not collected. It applies the same chapter/quest visibility, completion, team-lock and `canStartTasks` predicates as the full snapshot, and sorts by unsigned quest ID before selecting options. Its count consistency, fixed scope, sorted unique options and maximum-five option invariant are validated. It is not a partially collected `QuestSnapshot` mislabeled complete.
- **Planning and graph boundary:** `planForNext` requests the overview while deliberately marking detailed quest observation unavailable. `KnowledgeGraph` emits an `OBSERVATION_UNAVAILABLE` edge with that reason instead of inventing an empty observed quest graph. Operator debug-plan and debug-quest routes retain the full snapshot API. The selected recipe/material/execution logic is unchanged by this routing.
- **Readiness versus observation:** the capability probe checks supported APIs and existing team progress without traversing the quest book. Its successful detail explicitly says that the quest book and progress details were not collected. Commands that need quest state still perform a separate overview or full observation; they do not turn readiness into an observed empty book. The capability detail remains visible through `/companion capabilities` and structured output.
- **Optional linkage and failure:** the same exact-version gate runs before the snapshot adapter or readiness callback. Missing FTB remains `not_integrated`; unsupported versions remain unavailable. Runtime, optional-linkage and recursive-graph stack failures retain their cause in diagnostics and produce unavailable data. Null probe results cannot become successful capability observations. Public entry points enforce logical-server-thread access.
- **Identity and validation:** `HexFormat` emits the same 16-digit uppercase unsigned representation as the pinned FTB `%016X` formatter, including signed-long boundary values. The immutable precompiled regexes use `matches`, preserving complete-string, ASCII and uppercase constraints. The patch does not weaken snapshot consistency validation or immutable collection copies.
- **Bounds:** the 250 ms cooperative deadline remains unchanged and now includes readiness, collection and final snapshot construction/validation. Group, chapter, quest, task, dependency and text caps remain in force. Exceeding a bound discards the partial result and reports unavailable. The final time check occurs after the complete DTO constructor.
- **Diagnostics and privacy:** collection diagnostics contain bounded outcome/count/phase/timing fields. They do not log player identity, coordinates, quest titles, item lists or progression contents. The new code adds no network transmission, file export, task submission, quest completion or team mutation.

The reused static observations contain immutable adapter-limit explanations only. They do not cache any player's facts. The cached `OptionalQuestAccess` function is a stateless adapter entry point, not a cached snapshot.

## Tests inspected

The pure tests compare the new ID formatter with the pinned `%016X` representation for signed boundary values and deterministic random IDs. Validator tests include lowercase/full-width characters, trailing newline/whitespace, malformed namespaces and overlong IDs. Readiness and overview-gate tests prove that absent/unsupported versions do not invoke optional code, that these routes do not construct the full snapshot adapter, and that null/error results remain unavailable with diagnostics. Overview model tests cover immutable round trips, explicit omission of task fields, contradictory counts/locks, required option coverage and unique sorted IDs. The graph regression checks the explicit unavailable-details edge.

The generated real-FTB fixture constructs 4,790 quests, 9,580 item tasks and 66 chapters through the actual pinned FTB API. Its revised sequence calls the overview before any full observation of those new definitions, then compares its counts/options against a successful complete snapshot. It verifies same-tick partial progress, completion, team lock and definition-title/deletion changes. Detailed observations may time out without exposing partial data; the test requires at least one successful full observation within four separate bounded attempts, not universal cold full-export success. The existing smaller real-FTB fixture retains dependency-operator, completion and party-team-switch coverage. Synthetic-player and unresolved-team readiness are also checked.

The large fixture clearly labels itself as generated definitions, not the actual ATM10 book. Its simple item tasks and dependency chains of at most eight do not reproduce every custom task or visibility graph in ATM10. The fixture cannot replace an actual-pack retest.

## Limits of the review

A cooperative deadline cannot interrupt a single slow or recursively expensive FTB API call, class initialization, GC pause or logging operation. It must not be described as a hard 250 ms latency guarantee. The snapshot is a short request-time observation, not an atomic freeze of wall-clock-dependent repeatability. Overview calls retain group/chapter/quest and time bounds; they do not extract task lists, although FTB's own visibility predicates may consult tasks internally. Full-book JSON serialization is not included in the collection budget; production exports remain separately paged and bounded. The full debug snapshot can still exceed the collection budget and must report unavailable truthfully.

No authoritative revision covering all FTB progress and definition changes was found in the pinned release. Avoiding a live-progress cache is therefore material to this review's freshness conclusion. See `docs/M3.2-QUEST-RESEARCH.md` for the source evidence.

## Runtime evidence inspected

The reviewer inspected `evidence-m32/quest-production-baseline.json`: the old 0.3.1 observer was exercised against the disposable official ATM10 server pack, using a synthetic logged-in team rather than the player's world. Three samples were unavailable at 255.7, 250.3 and 250.1 ms. A fourth returned available at 267.8 ms with 66 chapters, 4,790 quests, 6,024 tasks and 5,231 dependencies. These are external request timings; the old code did not provide phase timings. Source review independently establishes that its final DTO construction/validation was outside its last deadline check. The new check closes that unchecked publication path; it does not turn the cooperative deadline into a hard external response-time guarantee.

The initial allocation-only repair still timed out on a cold generated large-book detailed request; warmed detailed requests were faster. This is why the final normal-command route uses a narrower explicit overview instead of promising that a complete detailed book always fits the deadline. A later fixture attempt also demonstrated that `FTB.clearCachedData()` after a definition edit can make the detailed scan cold again. The final test preserves the cold-overview requirement and allows up to four separately recorded, same-tick bounded attempts at that changed full snapshot. Unavailable attempts must contain no data; eventual success must match the changed title, count and deletion. This is an explicit change of observation contract, not an increase of the production deadline or a removal of the existing small-book detailed assertions. Source inspection confirms extra cold FTB title formatting, but the limited JFR sample did not establish that formatting as the dominant measured cost. No such profiling conclusion is claimed.

The reviewer subsequently inspected the completed `m32-verification-final.log`, all 19 final JUnit XML suites, and the copied aggregate evidence. The final clean Gradle run completed successfully in **2m 22s**. Its unit-test task was `FROM-CACHE`; the restored reports contain **130 tests, zero failures, errors or skips**. The runtime tasks executed and passed **26 core GameTests in 13.11s** and **3 FTB GameTests in 7.205s**. See `VERIFICATION.md` for the exact command and environment.

| Evidence | Measured result | Scope |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `evidence-m32/ftb-large-book.json` | First overview 36.712 ms; five subsequent summaries 5.865–24.044 ms; all available. | Generated 4,790-quest/9,580-task fixture plus 30 retained fixture quests, totaling 4,820 quests. The first overview precedes full observation of the newly created definitions. |
| Same large fixture | First full observation unavailable at 251.247 ms; later complete samples 152.619, 122.562 and 105.716 ms. | A full cold export is still allowed to time out safely. Same-tick partial progress, completion, lock/unlock and title/deletion equivalence assertions passed. The fixture restored its original 10 chapters/30 quests. |
| `evidence-m32/quest-production-optimized.json` | Four overviews available at **92.206, 25.555, 43.658 and 23.468 ms**. | Official ATM10 server pack, production loader, Companion 0.3.2, 503 loaded mods, synthetic logged-in team in the disposable test world. Real book: 66 chapters/4,790 quests; each overview returned five options. |

The ordinary-command repair does not imply that full exports always succeed on their first call. |

These external request timings include overhead outside the adapter's measured phases. They are samples on this host, not a latency guarantee. The official-pack synthetic team is not the user's team, and the dedicated server is not the user's integrated-client process.

## Focused actual-world and release verification

After the root engineer completed the authorized graphical playtest, the reviewer independently checked the focused record, retained aggregate diagnostics, and matching targeted lines in the actual instance's current client log. The log confirms Companion 0.3.2 loaded and recipe generation 2 published after a startup table replacement, without requiring another reload. The first Companion quest overview of the launch succeeded at **23:49:21.991** with **29.0121 ms** collector time; `/companion next` succeeded at **23:51:53.104** with **24.1512 ms** collector time. Both observed all **66 chapters/4,790 quests** and reported 179 completed, 4,400 available incomplete and 211 blocked/hidden/locked. The next-action chat confirms `already_owned` and `not_needed` for the diamond-pickaxe goal.

No matching Companion quest-timeout or knowledge/planning failure diagnostic was found through the last verified command at **23:51:53 local time on 22 September 2026**. This verifies the specific command timeout repair and preserved startup recovery in the user's integrated world. It does not establish a completely cold FTB internal cache, deep dependency planning, full debug-export reliability, multiplayer or every custom quest task. See `docs/M3.2-REAL-PLAYTEST.md` for deployment, environment and playtest boundaries.

The release audit confirmed the production JAR hash `393a37838bcaf9b962722b62e11df87e0ff1a6e64c0ed325cddd6a8223e21287`, 121 entries, and no bundled optional dependencies, Minecraft classes, test/probe classes or nested JARs. The inspected ZIP had 239 entries, included both historical and current playtest documents at their linked locations, and contained no forbidden cache, runtime, world/save or JFR paths/extensions. The packaging script checks those exclusions and production-JAR identity. The root engineer repackages after final documentation edits so this review is included. No raw user-world files or unrelated player data were added by this review.
